help.assignexecuser: Specifies the Job initiator UUID. The Job is created with that user's identity and permissions. The current authenticated user is used when omitted. When isSync is true, the current authenticated user is always used and this parameter is not supported.
help.combopname: Specifies the Combination Tool to run. The service finds it by name and builds the Job from its active version.
help.executeuser: Specifies the account used to connect to remote targets, not the Job initiator. A supplied value overrides the Combination Tool setting; otherwise, the Combination Tool setting is used.
help.invokeid: Specifies the invocation source ID that associates the caller with the Job for source tracing, queries, and callbacks. The active Combination Tool version ID is used when omitted.
help.ipportlist: Specifies the Job targets as a string array. Each item uses IP, IP:port, or IP:port/name. A non-empty array overrides the Combination Tool target configuration; an empty or omitted array uses the Combination Tool setting. Example: ["192.168.1.10","192.168.1.11:22","192.168.1.12:2222/app"].
help.issync: Controls whether the API waits for the Job result. false returns the Job ID after creation and trigger-mode setup. true immediately runs the Job as the current authenticated user and waits for termination or the listener timeout before returning status and node output. A listener timeout does not terminate the Job.
help.name: Specifies the Job name used for display and queries. Duplicate names are allowed. The Combination Tool name is used when omitted or blank.
help.parallelcount: Specifies the number of targets that may run concurrently. It is used only when parallelPolicy is parallel and ignored by other policies. The Combination Tool setting is used when omitted; the default is 32 when the tool also has no value.
help.parallelpolicy: Specifies the target concurrency policy. parallel uses parallelCount; roundCount divides targets into batches and uses roundCount. The Combination Tool setting is used when omitted.
help.param: Specifies Job parameters as key-value pairs. Each key should match a Job parameter key defined by the active Combination Tool version. Missing parameters use the tool defaults and are converted by parameter type; an empty JSON object is used when omitted. Example: {"paramKey":"paramValue"}.
help.parentid: Specifies the parent Job ID and associates the current Job as its child. The parent Job must exist, and the parent chain supports at most two levels.
help.planstarttime: Specifies the planned start time as a Unix timestamp in milliseconds. When triggerType is auto and the time is in the future, the Job runs automatically at that time. This parameter is not supported when isSync is true.
help.protocol: Specifies the protocol name used to connect to remote targets, such as ssh. A supplied value overrides the Combination Tool setting; creation is rejected when the protocol does not exist. The tool setting is used when omitted.
help.roundcount: Specifies the number of batches used to divide the targets. It is used only when parallelPolicy is roundCount and ignored by other policies. The Combination Tool setting is used when omitted; the default is 64 when the tool also has no value.
help.runnergroup: Specifies the Runner group name or ID used to match and dispatch the Job. -1 selects a group at random. The Combination Tool setting is used when omitted.
help.runnergrouptag: Specifies Runner group tag names or IDs used to filter eligible groups. Use a single tag or a JSON-array string of tags. A group must satisfy both the tags and routing rules. The Combination Tool setting is used when omitted.
help.scenarioname: Specifies the Combination Tool scenario whose configured stages will run. Creation is rejected when the scenario does not exist. The tool's default execution scope is used when omitted.
help.triggertype: Specifies how the Job is triggered. auto runs immediately or at planStartTime; manual creates the Job and waits for a manual trigger. The Job runs immediately when omitted. This parameter is not supported when isSync is true.

desc.main:
This tool performs semantic retrieval within the configured knowledge bases and returns the knowledge snippets most relevant to the user question.
It applies to product documentation Q&A, operation guide retrieval, rule knowledge lookup, and similar scenarios.
If the current question clearly depends on knowledge base content, call this tool before answering.

Returned result structure:
1. The returned object contains:
- matches: hit result list
- bestMatch: best hit result, with the same structure as an item in matches

2. Each item in matches contains these common fields:
- datasetId: knowledge base ID
- datasetName: knowledge base name
- handler: knowledge base handler name
- chunkId: hit chunk ID
- sourceId: source record ID
- objectId: business object ID
- objectType: business object type
- name: business object name
- content: matched text snippet
- status: chunk status
- score: match score
- meta: knowledge base custom extension information

yamlhelp.control: Control configuration uses the existing graphical schema. Matrices, resource filters and validation rules retain their existing protocols; shared data sources are not edited here.
yamlhelp.execute: Use the graphical options applicable to this level. parallelPolicy=parallel uses parallelCount; roundCount uses the parent roundCount. These are mutually exclusive. A preset switch of 0 clears its preset settings. Runner constants use names; -1 means automatic assignment.
yamlhelp.group: Each phase group owns its strategy, batch size and execution settings. grayScale enables staged execution. List order determines group order; group numbers are internal.
yamlhelp.mapping: Write constants directly; references require explicit mappingMode/value. Ordinary ${...} strings remain constants. isempty omits value. Object constants containing mappingMode are rejected as ambiguous.
yamlhelp.node: Resources are identified by IP, port, name and resource type. Ambiguous matches require an unambiguous existing binding. Manual nodes need not exist in the Resource Center.
yamlhelp.operation: Select the operation by opName. IF-Block uses condition/if/else; LOOP-Block uses loopItems/loopItemVar/operations. Nested operations use the same structure. Write constants directly and references with mappingMode/value.
yamlhelp.param: Retain both the key and display name. type is the graphical control type. defaultValue and config use the existing control structure. Update references when changing or deleting a key.
yamlhelp.phase: phaseType is the graphical execution mode and is required for native-only phases. target and runner_target are compatible. execRound applies to runner/sqlfile phases in staged groups.
yamlhelp.protocol: Select an existing protocol by name and optional port. Provide the port to disambiguate. Protocol definitions and internal IDs cannot be edited.
yamlhelp.reference: Identify an upstream operation by phase, operation name and output parameter. Repeated operation references retain the system-provided opLetter address; it cannot edit the operation itself.
yamlhelp.root: Full version configuration. Each runFlow entry is a phase group. Basic information, permissions and notifications are outside this snapshot.
yamlhelp.scenario: Select an existing scenario by name and associate phase names. This changes version bindings only, not shared scenario definitions.
yamlhelp.target: Use the existing Resource Center filter structure. Selected resources, manual nodes, filters, runtime parameters and upstream output are mutually exclusive. Runtime parameters accept display names or keys.

reportprocesstasktool.description:
Use this tool to submit a Task.
1. A Task must be submitted through a Service. Parameters vary by Service, so call SERVICE_REPORT_PARAM_LIST with the Service name to obtain them.
2. If the user has not specified a Service, call the tool that lists the Services available to the current user and ask for a Service name.
3. After the user provides partial data, call SERVICE_REPORT_PARAM_LIST again, validate every required parameter, and request missing values.
4. When all required data is available, call this tool to submit the Task.
5. If submission fails, return the failure reason.
6. If submission succeeds, return a link to the Task details page. The link template is ${homeUrl}/process.html#/task-detail?processTaskId=${processTaskId}. Replace the variables with returned data. Do not display the raw URL; generate a linked Task title that opens in a new window.
7. Use this JSON structure for form data: {"formAttributeDataList":[{"key":"form attribute key","label":"form attribute label","dataList":"user-provided form attribute value"}]}.
8. Do not modify user input or insert spaces between Chinese, English, or numeric characters.
